chunks: Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the milk of camels, sheep, and cows, and their urines and their flesh. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not perform wudu from it if anything of it hits you, or your clothes, so do not wash it unless you wish to clean it.'

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the urines of beasts, mules, and donkeys. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wash it. If you do not know its place, wash the entire garment. And if you doubt, sprinkle it (with water).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing clothes stained with the urine of different animals in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'original purity' (al-asl fi al-ashya' al-taharah) by distinguishing between animals whose urine is ritually pure (like camels and cattle) and those that are impure (like donkeys and mules). It provides practical legal guidance on the extent of purification required, ranging from no action needed for pure animals to full washing or sprinkling (tanazzuh) for impure ones, reflecting the nuanced approach to fiqh al--imam. This distinction is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the validity of prayer when impurities are encountered.
